title: Same-index coherent scalarReduction for every normalized scalar model
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with embedding $\iota:E\to L$, a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and an integral derived-complete constructible object $A\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $R_E=\varprojlim_m(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $A_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$, $B_m=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)_W$, $B_{L/E}$ for the completed scalar extension with its same-index coefficient maps $A_{E,m}\to B_m$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $R_E,R_L$ also for derived coherent reduction to quotient systems [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Let $S_Y$ be any normalized primitive scalar model for $E\to L$ on $W$, in the prime/finite-field/embedding/scheme setting of [lem-trf-primitive-quotient-scalar-model-existence], and use the coefficient-extension reduction model of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model]. Then the coherent comparison
$$\operatorname{scalarReduction}_{S_Y}(A):R_L(B_{L/E}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{E,L}(A)$$
obtained by applying $R_L$ to the realization isomorphism of $S_Y$ and then the coherent counit is invertible, where $C_{E,L}(A)$ is the normalized [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] coherent $\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1}$-system whose $n$th term is $A\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1})$. Under the tower-data identification of [def-pur-scalar-extension-tower-data], this is the same coherent-reduction isomorphism $\gamma_A:R_L(B_{L/E}A)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{L/E}(R_EA)$. Let $P\to A$ be a flat-term K-flat representative over $R_E$. For every $n\geq0$, its component is the coherent counit induced by
$$(P\otimes_{R_E}A_{E,n+1})\otimes_{A_{E,n+1}}B_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\ (x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab\ }P\otimes_{R_E}B_{n+1},$$
so both source and target use the quotient $B_{n+1}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{n+1}$ at the same index $n$. There is no replacement of $n$ by $e(L/E)n$; ramification is already in the recorded quotient map.
